title: Solving Systems with Real Eigenvalues

blocks.html: For one equation $y' = ay$ the solution is $ce^{at}$. For a system $\mathbf{x}' = A\mathbf{x}$ we look for solutions of the same shape, $\mathbf{x} = e^{\lambda t}\mathbf{v}$, a fixed vector whose length grows or shrinks exponentially. This is where eigenvalues and diagonalization meet differential equations.

$\mathbf{x} = e^{\lambda t}\mathbf{v}$ solves $\mathbf{x}' = A\mathbf{x}$ exactly when $A\mathbf{v} = \lambda\mathbf{v}$. If a $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ has real eigenvalues $\lambda_1 \ne \lambda_2$ with eigenvectors $\mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_2$, then $$\mathbf{x}(t) = c_1e^{\lambda_1t}\mathbf{v}_1 + c_2e^{\lambda_2t}\mathbf{v}_2.$$

Substituting $\mathbf{x} = e^{\lambda t}\mathbf{v}$: the left side is $\lambda e^{\lambda t}\mathbf{v}$ and the right side is $e^{\lambda t}A\mathbf{v}$. Cancelling the nonzero scalar $e^{\lambda t}$ leaves $A\mathbf{v} = \lambda\mathbf{v}$. The eigenvalues solve $\det(A - \lambda I)$ $= \lambda^{2} - (\operatorname{tr}A)\lambda + \det A = 0$. Superposition combines the two straight-line solutions, and since $\mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_2$ are independent, the constants can match any $\mathbf{x}(0)$. In the eigenvector coordinates the system splits into two separate equations, $u_1' = \lambda_1u_1$ and $u_2' = \lambda_2u_2$.

blocks.title: A zero eigenvalue
blocks.a: $x_1 = 2 + 2e^{-2t}$, $x_2 = 2 - 2e^{-2t}$: both settle at 2, sharing the total equally

blocks.html: Scaling an eigenvector is fine (any nonzero multiple works), but mixing up which eigenvector goes with which eigenvalue is not: each $e^{\lambda_it}$ must multiply its own $\mathbf{v}_i$. Check one column: $A\mathbf{v}_1$ should equal $\lambda_1\mathbf{v}_1$.

blocks.name: phaseplane
blocks.cap: Trajectories of $\mathbf{x}' = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\mathbf{x}$. Along the purple eigen-directions solutions move in straight lines: outward along $(1, 1)$ (growth $e^{3t}$) and inward along $(1, -1)$ (decay $e^{-t}$). Every other path bends from one direction toward the other.
